_units._note: ALL SIZES IN THIS FILE ARE SCREEN PIXELS AT 1x, or TILES where the key says _tiles. The builder converts. Height and plan use DIFFERENT constants: world height projects at cos(60)*36.9502 = 18.4752 px per tile, ground depth at sin(60)*36.9502 = 32.0 px per tile. So height_px 6 means 6/18.4752 = 0.3248 world units, and a ground shape is 1:1 with tile width. Stated here so nobody re-derives them, and so nobody uses the wrong one.

_hue_rule: VEGETATION MUST BE GREENER THAN THE GROUND, OR EQUAL. NEVER YELLOWER. Ground #2E3A26 is hue 96; vegetation sits 96-115. Yellow is for dead terrain, and there is no dead terrain yet. Gated on the RENDERED sprite by art/tools/assert_doodad_hue.py, not on the albedo, because the key light is warm (1.0, 0.965, 0.912) and drags hue toward yellow - an albedo inside the window can still render outside it. The retired grass_tuft rendered at hue 38.7, which is 57 degrees warm of the ground, and that is exactly why it read as straw.
_vegetation_is_not_a_machine_material: The locked natural-5 palette is a MACHINE-MATERIALS palette - fieldstone, wrought iron, weathered oak, leather, verdigris - and not one member lands in the vegetation hue window. Oak is hue 29.5, verdigris 152.7; fieldstone is 100 but it is a grey, so as grass it reads as gravel. Vegetation therefore derives from the GROUND's own hue family rather than from lock.PALETTE. Grass is terrain, not equipment. Pebbles are mineral and keep fieldstone: the hue rule binds vegetation only.
_gate: THREE bounds. VALUE: (1) median <= ground * median_cap - does it read as an object; (2) p95 <= pooled building p50, measured each run - no part of a decoration is as bright as the typical part of a machine. These trade automatically, since p95 ~= median * sqrt(internal range), so a busier form is pushed darker. Internal shading range is UNCONSTRAINED. HUE: (3) rendered hue inside hue_window, vegetation only. The value bounds are a CEILING, not a target - they stop a set shouting over the buildings, they cannot make a bad set good.
_placement: FOR THE GAME SIDE, NOT THE RENDERER. Patches go down CLUSTERED, never uniform. Hash a low-frequency mask over world position and place patches only where the mask is high, leaving the rest bare. Density VARIANCE is what reads as ground; uniform scatter is what reads as sprinkled confetti. Suggested: patch A and B at high mask values, patch C around their edges as the fade-out, pebble_cluster as a rare accent at roughly 1 per 40 tiles and independent of the vegetation mask.

_schema.name: output basename; renders to art/sprites/doodads/<name>.png
_schema.kind: 'patch' (a multi-tile clump of vegetation) or 'ground' (lies flat on the ground plane)
_schema.size_tiles: [width, depth] of a patch footprint, in tiles
_schema.height_px: blade height in FINAL screen pixels; converted to world Z by px / 18.4752
_schema.blades: how many blades in the patch. This is density, not decoration - a patch is dense overlapping vegetation, not a few objects standing near each other
_schema.shape: 'round' (radial falloff), 'lobed' (two overlapping centres), 'sparse' (low flat density, edge-of-patch)
_schema.plan_px: ground doodads only: plan width in final pixels
_schema.plan_squash: Y scale on the plan shape. 1.0 = true plan, and it stays 1.0: the camera squashes the ground by GROUND_SQUASH and the anamorphic downsample stretches it back, so ground shapes already arrive at true proportions. Measured on _calib_disc, 1:1 within a pixel. See PIPELINE.md 34.
_schema.materials: vegetation_palette names for patches, lock.PALETTE names for mineral doodads
_schema.seed: deterministic RNG seed. The same seed must give the same doodad forever, or the sprite changes under people who have approved it
_schema.albedo_value_scale: scalar on linear albedo, solved by art/tools/calibrate_doodads.py. Uniform across RGB, so hue is preserved and only brightness is given up
_schema.rarity_per_tiles: advisory placement density for the game side: roughly one of these per N tiles

doodads.name: _calib_disc
doodads.note: A flat unit-diameter disc lying on the ground. Renders through the exact doodad path so the plan aspect ratio can be MEASURED rather than derived. Comes back 32x33 at alpha>127 and 32x31 at alpha>200 - 1:1 within a pixel - which is what settled plan_squash at 1.0. Permanent fixture, never regenerated, never used in game.

doodads.name: _calib_dome
doodads.note: A flat-shaded hemisphere: every normal a ground doodad can present, under the locked rig. Its rendered p95/p5 luminance IS the rig diffuse dynamic range - measured 2.72:1 - and therefore the floor under any contrast ratio a rounded form can reach. Permanent fixture, never regenerated, never used in game.

doodads.name: ground_cover_patch_A
doodads.note: The workhorse patch. Dense overlapping blades on a radial falloff, so it is solid at the centre and breaks up at the rim - and the broken rim is what lets two patches overlap without reading as a tile seam.

doodads.name: ground_cover_patch_B
doodads.note: Two overlapping centres rather than one, so a field of A and B does not read as a single shape repeated. Wider than deep, which is also the cheaper direction on screen.

doodads.name: ground_cover_patch_C
doodads.note: Edge-of-patch. Sparse and low, meant to be scattered around A and B so a patch fades into bare ground instead of ending at an outline. Not a standalone object - placed alone it is the confetti problem again.

doodads.name: pebble_cluster
doodads.note: KEPT from the first set and demoted to a rare mineral accent, roughly 1 per 40 tiles, placed independently of the vegetation mask. Mineral, so the vegetation hue rule does not bind it.
